neighbours.label: weld and sewing seams: the joint line where two pieces of material are joined (weld, seam allowance)
fire: Before painting, the inspector checked each weld for porosity and cracks.
When sewing the panels, leave a half-inch seam allowance on every edge.
The fabricator ground the weld flush so the joint would be invisible.
Trim the seam allowance to reduce bulk before turning the collar out.
Poor weld penetration is the most common cause of bracket failure.
With a quarter-inch foot, the quilter keeps every seam perfectly even.
X-ray testing confirms that the weld has no hidden voids.
After stitching, press the seam flat so the blocks lie neatly together.
quiet: Before painting, the inspector checked each beam for rust and dents.
When sewing the panels, choose a strong thread that matches the fabric.
The fabricator polished the steel so the frame would shine.
Trim the loose threads before turning the collar out.
Poor bolt tightening is the most common cause of bracket failure.
With a walking foot, the quilter can sew thick layers easily.
X-ray testing confirms that the casting has no hidden voids.
After stitching, fold the blocks so they lie neatly in the basket.

notes: Card: peaks ' weld', ' seam' x2, ' surface' x5, ' edge', 'compressive', 'adhesion', 縫製. Probe: weld 0.46, seam allowance 0.49, paint adhesion 0.23, glue bond 0.14, solder joint 0.06, sanding the surface only 0.02. Shirt ironing 0.10, truck leaks 0.02. Only weld and seam reliably fire, so the label is that narrow joint-line meaning rather than surfaces in general. Near misses keep welding/sewing settings without the joint word.
